# Canary full context

Updated: 2026-11-24 13:22 CET

Version 3.46 adds `canary market read --json` (MCP `canary_market_read`): the
S&P 500 against the prior session's high and low, SPY volume against the same
time of day in prior sessions, VIX against its 25 line and the largest
companies against their opening gaps, with tags that name a condition only
once it holds for two completed five-minute closes, a tag timeline, and before
the open an indication from the ES and NQ futures and the leaders' pre-market
prices; every threshold is returned and marked heuristic. `add market` and
`add call-plan` size a put on a Rulebook hedge symbol against the book's long
exposure under rule 12's over-hedge line (`index_protection`,
`hedge_room_contracts`). `canary strategies spreads`, `strategies spread-plan`
and `strategies open --units N --limit DEBIT` price, size and, with `--submit`, send a bull call
or bear put spread as one combination order; credit, ratio, calendar and
uncovered shapes are refused, and a held spread counts at its net value in the
loss measure. None has yet been sent to a live broker. An `exit_plan` in
`canary proposals queue prepare --stdin`, armed with the owner's signature, sells a
held long call after the open and when its stock falls back to a trailing
line, with `validity` `day`, `Nd` or `gtc`; it carries over sessions, rests at
the mid on a quote wider than its spread limit, and covers only the calls
outside a Canary spread. Orders show a combination's legs and a trailing
stop's current trigger (`trail.stop_price`). The mandate charges a long line
with too little history at its whole value instead of going unknown, and the
day's first fills explain an equity move.
Version 3.45 adds `canary add search PATTERN [--json]`, a read-only lookup
through IBKR's symbol search by symbol or company name that names each
listing's currency and the exchange Add asks on (IBKR connections only). A
stock add whose quantity is off the broker's board lot is held with
`add_lot_size`, and `--max` sizes in whole lots; `add` market detail carries
`min_size` and `size_increment`. The `[cash.sweep]` key
`buy_stock_on_borrowed_currency` (off unless written) lets a stock purchase
borrow its own currency while the account's free cash in every currency, after
floats, open purchases and the reserve, still covers it; each such order
carries the warning `add_borrowed_currency` with the borrowed amount, and
`--max` never borrows. An entry the broker never acknowledged is cancelled
once when its attached stop is refused, and an order record the broker never
acknowledged is bound or closed by the reconcile sweep. Option entries sized
by `add`, strategy previews and combination broker previews no longer fail
inside Canary; orders carry the contract multiplier in the type IBKR reads, no
empty attached-orders field, and combination legs with IBKR's default leg
fields. None of these option or combination orders has yet been sent to a live
broker. Regime readings label a
previous-session close as such, gamma never takes it as spot, and the daemon
prunes old damaged-store copies and schema-upgrade backups after a start.
Version 3.44 adds `canary strategies add ID REVISION --units N`, which buys
whole units of a held option strategy as one combination order, every leg in
the held ratio, at a day limit, from the command line only (a preview
unless `--submit` is given); no proposal and no app route sends one. The order is judged
once: a covered combination (every sold contract capped by a bought one of
the same kind, expiry, size and trading class nearer the money) is held to
the order cap on its net premium and needs no `allow_option_sell_to_open`; a
covered put combination on a hedge symbol, or one covering no more shares
than are held, is a hedge entry the brake and the mandate leave open; any
other combination is held to the gross premium, the permission, the brake,
the mandate and the premium limits. A held strategy trades as whole units:
a proposal for one leg is blocked with `strategy_workflow_required`, the
protection trim proposes whole units, `canary proposals reduce` leaves out a
long option held against a sold one, and an exercise of such an option is
listed blocked. Strategies carry a name beside their kind, and a butterfly,
an iron condor, an iron butterfly, a covered call and a collar are
recognised. Premium at risk counts a spread at what the pair can lose; index
protection is sized by the pair's short delta; protection premium is not
counted in the premium budget, the per-name limit or the option buy check;
the premium budget shows it in a note.
Version 3.43 starts the daemon through launchd on macOS, so it no longer
belongs to the app that started it. macOS ends the processes an app started when that app quits or updates
itself and may not leave background processes behind; a daemon started from
an app, or from a terminal inside one, went down with it and left no line in
its log. `canary restart`, and so the restart after `canary update`, installs
a per-user launchd agent, `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.osauer.canary-daemon.plist`,
and from then on `canary` starts the daemon through it. The daemon starts at
login and exits after the idle time if nothing uses it; launchd starts it
again after a crash or a forced kill; a stop the user asked for stays a stop.
macOS lists the agent among its background items. A program that was already running before the update keeps
starting the daemon directly until that program is restarted. There is one
agent per user, for the configuration that installed it: a daemon with its
own `CANARY_SOCKET`, other `XDG_*` directories or another config file, or one
started over SSH without a desktop session, is started directly, as on Linux,
where nothing changes. `canary daemon --remove-agent` removes the agent once
the daemon is stopped. With a `[mandate]` table the drawdown brake reads the
mandate's high-water mark as its peak: a new high counts once a second
reading at least five minutes later confirms it, at the lower of the two.
Before, the brake's own peak rose on a single reading, so the brake could
block before the mandate's maximum loss was reached. The brake then counts only the fall since the mandate's high, and the
change can only move a block later. A peak the user lowered with
`reset-drawdown` or `correct-peak` still applies while it is the lower one;
the warn and block percentages and how a block clears are unchanged, and
without a mandate nothing changes. Version 3.42.1: a Regime indicator
that had confirmed keeps its confirmation while its own reading is not due
(USD/JPY in its pause, gamma from the options close to the next open); a row
older than its group's age bound is not a current rating; a Cboe volatility
file overdue for more than four days counts as a concern.

Version 3.42 makes `canary status` and `canary edge` answer first.
`canary status` prints whether you can trade under its headline, then three
groups: Broker, Trading and Canary. Its phone push row states one fact and
`canary app status` keeps the delivery history. `canary status --details`
adds the broker's API settings, read on a separate short-lived connection; it
replaces `--gateway-diagnostics`, which is removed. `canary edge` opens with a
bottom line (the account result, how graded stock decisions and closed option
positions split, and the review's one finding), then option trades by kind,
the largest single decisions and how much of the history is scored;
`canary edge --details` is the full review, and `--change`, `--option` and
the paging flags show it too. These view changes leave JSON, the MCP tools
and the app as they were. Edge carries seven forward tests;
`forward_tests[].sample` counts a rule's decisions executed after its
registration for five of them, and two are registered but not yet counted.
`canary edge tests` shows each test's question, count and expected date.
Canary counts and does not answer them: no verdict, grade, warning or order
depends on them. A sale test says how many of its sales Canary's protection
sent, and an option spread is left out because one leg misreads it. The daemon writes each US session's
Regime stage and premium budget level itself, without waiting for a reader.
Regime rates a reading from a shut market as current when no newer one can
exist, each monitor row carries `current`, and an input outage that hides a
confirmation blanks the stage instead of letting it read calmer. Data health:
one instrument failing no longer marks the quote or history feed unhealthy,
an expected delay alone no longer makes `canary status` read ATTENTION, the
trading-halts feed is not due while US markets are closed, and IBKR's
Saturday Flex maintenance is an expected delay for the statement it delays.

Version 3.41 adopts policy files left in the old directory. Through v3.34.1
the four policy files lived in `~/.config/ibkr/policies`; v3.35.0 moved their
default under `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and stopped reading the old directory, so a
daemon with another config directory ran on Canary's defaults in place of the
user's limits, and orders its protection policy pre-authorises were not
placed. At its first start on v3.41.0 such a daemon copies the files to its
own directory, only when its own record shows it ran on them; the record
covers the risk policy and the Rulebook policy, so a user who changed only the
protection or opportunity policy copies the directory by hand, as does one
whose daemon log shows no "adopted" line after the update. A second daemon
with its own config directory keeps its own policies. Untouched defaults at
the new place are replaced and kept as a backup; where the file at the new
place already carries the user's settings neither is replaced, `canary policy
show --explain` names both, and the user merges them by hand. `canary policy
ensure` writes no default where the old directory holds the file. Edge
registers six forward tests for each account: `forward_tests` lists each rule
with its text, `rule_hash` and `registered_at`, only decisions executed after
`registered_at` belong to a rule's sample, and the record survives updates,
restarts and rebuilt reviews; `forward_tests_unavailable` says when it could
not be read. Canary registers the rules and reads none: no verdict, grade,
warning or order depends on them. At the first Regime read after each US close
and before midnight New York the daemon records the stage Regime served and
the Rulebook's premium budget act level, once and never rewritten; a
decision's detail serves them as `prior_session` and `decision_session`. An
option's sessions are counted on its own market's days: for a US-listed option
the days SPY, QQQ or DIA has a close; an option whose statement names no US
option exchange, and any option while no such close is on record, has no
session score (`session_calendar_unavailable`). A stock quote read waits about
250 ms at most for a new line's bid, ask and last, so `canary add` no longer
prices from a lone bid while the ask and last are still arriving. A background
account read no longer holds up price updates while a store write runs, and a
book held for missing positions warns once per episode.

Version 3.40 extends Edge to options. An option decision gets the same 1, 5
and 20-session score as a stock decision: from IBKR's daily statement value
while the contract is held and, once it has left the account, from the
contract's closing bid/ask midpoint, read from IBKR while the contract is
alive. No price is estimated. Each option score's `close_source` says which:
`statement_mark` or `closing_quote`. A stock or ETF decision carries a verdict
(helped, hurt, no_difference, or none with a reason) from the 5-session score
after costs and from nothing else; `verdicts.counts` counts them. An option
decision carries no verdict: each completed option position in
`options.cycles` has one `grade`, made_money, lost_money or flat, by the sign
of the result IBKR booked for the whole position, and none after an exercise
or assignment or when that result is incomplete. An expiry is how a position
closed, not a decision. Each option decision instead carries `position`, a
fact and not a grade: a trade that opened or added to the position is compared
with the average price its contracts were closed at (contracts still held at
the latest statement value), a trade that reduced or closed it with the
average entry price. `verdicts.recent` lists the 20 newest decisions; `canary
edge` prints the ten newest. A later trade in the same stock or ETF no longer
removes a score, so Edge totals from earlier versions are not comparable. The
Regime stage vote gives each of its eight rows a role: the VIX term structure,
VVIX, the funding spread and cash credit spreads are stress witnesses and
start a warning; the ETF credit proxy, USD/JPY, dealer gamma and breadth are
co-signs and count only beside a confirmed red witness. Panic needs a fall in
SPY, VVIX turns red at 120, an unreadable witness beside a yellow or red
co-sign reads early warning, and a volatility row, funding and cash credit
spreads all confirmed red send the stress alert on a flat market. The trading
rulebook applies its calm limits on the days Regime now reads quiet. A market
data line request ends with its broker session, a failed line cancel is sent
again, and a gamma compute stuck past 30 minutes is abandoned, so one stuck
recompute no longer blocks the next. An unfilled forced reduction keeps its
limit while pre-authorised orders are paused, while the risk-budget overrun
behind it cannot be confirmed, and after its limit was changed through Canary.

Version 3.39 fixes a deadlock in the broker connection. After a burst of
order messages the daemon could stop reading the broker and never reconnect;
the reader now takes its locks in one order for every message family. A
shutdown that hangs ends the process after ten seconds, so `canary restart`
always takes over. A bill purchase passes the drawdown brake, as it already
passed the mandate gate, so a cash sweep can be sent while the brake is on.
A forced reduction the scheduler placed moves its limit to the current bid
when it stays unfilled, under two new `[mandate.reduction]` keys. When the
budget governor and the hedge trim ask to sell the same contracts of one
put, `canary proposals` lists one row with both reasons. A session's daily
bar is kept only from a read taken after its close has settled.

Version 3.38 moves the Go module to `github.com/osauer/canary/v3`. Every
release tag is now a Go module version, so `go get
github.com/osauer/canary/v3@latest` and pkg.go.dev give the current daemon
client and `pkg/ibkr`. The `/v2` path ends at v2.8.5; a program on it
changes its import paths to `/v3`, and some `pkg/ibkr` scanner calls were
removed after v2.8.5. The `canary` program behaves as in v3.37.

Version 3.37 counts a bought option in the mandate's loss measure at what it
is worth today. A long put on a hedge-listed index is protection, shown in
`verdict.loss.protection_base` beside the measure; the contracts past the
over-hedge line count, in `verdict.loss.protection_excess_base`, and so does
every such put once no long book is left. Canary offers to trim that excess
back to the hedge band, sent only on your confirmation. The order gate judges
a sale of anything but the hedge puts against the book without them, so a
forced reduction is no longer held to the option contract cap by its own
hedge. After TWS loses its link to IBKR, open orders are read again once the
link returns (tested against simulated outages).

Version 3.36 keeps the index to the database's write-ahead log in the daemon's
memory and holds daemon.db exclusively while it runs, so an older copy of
that index file can no longer stop orders with lost_write; another program's
open of daemon.db gets "database is locked". SEHK and SGX orders go to their
own exchange as plain limit orders, on their market's hours, tested so far
against a simulated broker only. On OpenD, still experimental, the regime,
portfolio stress and the market overview work in part and mark the inputs
OpenD cannot supply. The daemon refuses a request field its method does not
declare. Canary is built with Go 1.27.4, which fixes GO-2026-6859 in the HTTP
server of canary app.

Version 3.35 keeps the index hedge available when a book has used all of its
loss room: one rule now decides a sale, on the 10% fall and the 10% rise. A
forced reduction buys back a hedge that has passed neutral, and the hedge is
sized with working sales counted as sold. On accounts where the broker reports
an exchange rate of 1, reconciliation and the position download check use a
real rate.

Version 3.34 requires an arming before Canary places pre-authorised orders by
itself: a one-time confirmation on a paired device, Protection or Fully armed.
The forced reduction no longer sells long puts on the rulebook's hedge indexes,
and its nearest-expiry send order holds across veto windows.

Version 3.33 serves accounts that trade from Asia: Singapore, ASX and China
A-share calendars beside Hong Kong and Tokyo, a brief whose session row
follows the exchange holding most of the book, position figures in their
own currency, and a start page for Hong Kong and Singapore accounts. `canary
feedback` turns a defect into a redacted report and a prefilled GitHub bug
form link. The regime gate and strategy one's screen arrive as readings. Six
fixes in the TWS wire client correct legacy order status frames, position
multipliers, delayed-data notices and stale quote refreshes.

Version 3.32 counts working put purchases and share sales before a put can
qualify as protection, nets an index hedge against the index funds it
protects, and stores each distinct statement-row version once. Older
supported databases can complete their upgrade. The release also updates
the relay development tooling's vulnerable dependency and strengthens
source validation and the repository privacy check.

Version 3.31 adds protective puts to Add, with the call and put bands in
the opportunity policy. The volatility budget can be lifted from Desk's
console after a confirmation on the paired device. Canary's own privacy
check and log monitor no longer open the daemon's database. The daemon
also recovers from a lost save without a restart.

Version 3.30 lets you close an index hedge from Canary: `canary proposals
reduce --con-id ID --include-hedges` buys back held Micro E-mini S&P 500
futures. The hedge plan only suggests a sale Canary will accept and says
what's holding it back. A deleted hedge table stays deleted, and the daemon
clears out its own old policy backups.

Version 3.29 adds reduction-plan comparisons for index falls and rises, loss
room and quoted trading costs, plus index-hedge planning. Optional IV-fallback
policy reports uncertainty when a held option lacks its own volatility.
Plans are not submission authority.

Version 3.28 adds historical option-exit replay, option-list pagination and
intraday account-value history. Holding locks cover a name across its held
contracts. Mandate reporting separates the loss measure from volatility;
proposal reviews include an index-fall comparison when it can be measured.
Historical replays are not forecasts or instructions to trade.

Version 3.27 adds stock-entry reviews with optional protection for the added
shares, call discovery and budget-based call sizing, and holding locks for
bulk and automatic reductions. CLI help includes JSON request examples.
Reduction checks account for Canary's working combo legs and wait when known
fills and positions disagree. Existing written limits are preserved; policy
migration adds missing reduction-allowance fields (1% for stocks/ETFs and 5%
for options). Standard binaries and MCP remain read-only, and MCP cannot
preview or submit orders.

Version 3.26 says in plain words which TWS or IB Gateway settings differ
from what Canary needs: `canary status` gains a Gateway setup row, read once
after each connect, and Canary never changes a setting. When the Gateway
answers the open-order request late, as during IBKR's nightly reset, the
daemon now redials its connection instead of reading no open orders until a
restart. Existing policies load unchanged; standard binaries and MCP remain
read-only.

Version 3.25 lets every live strategy in the register trade, not only the
core: each entry written live turns its month's decision into a row of its
own on its own line, with the core's terms, gates and standing-mandate path,
and its fills count in its own sleeve. A strategy whose traded share class
is young can read its trend on an older class of the same fund until its
own closes fill the window. The second strategy, a managed-futures fund on
its EUR-hedged Xetra line, can be written into the register. Existing
policies load unchanged; standard binaries and MCP remain read-only.

Version 3.24 lets the desk's arming reach the strategies: Canary serves a
submit path for the standing automatic mandate the owner confirms once on
their device, so a controller can send a served strategy row, the core
sleeve's monthly buy included, through the one order path with every gate
re-checked; nothing is sent until the controller presents that mandate. The
decision scorecard can now conclude: one unit of evidence per name and week,
overlap charged, the market taken out on SPY and the sector fund, a placebo
and a futility test, and each decision's fill cost. The owner's sleeve gets a
drawdown stop of its own. Existing policies load unchanged; standard binaries
and MCP remain read-only.

Version 3.23 adds one strategy evaluator that runs every machine strategy in
the risk policy's register: the core sleeve's rule is its first entry,
unchanged, and a second strategy is a table naming its fund, a signal from the
library and the owner's numbers (`canary strategy ID` shows what it would
trade). The core sleeve can go live at a small stage: with its stage written,
each monthly decision becomes one proposal row the owner confirms on their
device, and the daemon never sends it by itself. Every entry runs in shadow
until the owner writes its stage. Existing policies load unchanged; standard
binaries and MCP remain read-only.

Version 3.22 adds the owner's mandate: a whole-book risk budget measured by
historical simulation, refusals of risk-adding orders while the book is over
it, a pre-authorised forced reduction with a veto window, and risk
allocations per sleeve. A decision scorecard scores every position change per
sleeve with sequential evidence, and a quote kept at every fill measures the
spread paid. A strategy register in the risk policy names each machine
strategy; the core sleeve runs read-only in shadow; an option-chain recorder
saves the desk's chains once a session. Hand orders in TWS can be cancelled or
changed from Canary when the owner enables it, and two Canary orders never
sell the same shares twice. Cash interest rates come from the broker's
statement. Existing policies load unchanged; standard binaries and MCP remain
read-only.

Version 3.21 adds owner-confirmed order queues and whole-position stock trailing
protection in trading builds. It fixes large volume readings and keeps explicitly
deactivated orders visible without counting them as active protection. A read-only
CLI diagnostic reports supported TWS and Gateway API settings as part of
TWS / IB Gateway 10.50 compatibility hardening. The main connection keeps its
tested protocol. Live validation used TWS; Gateway 10.50 still needs an end-to-end
check. Existing policies and broker settings stay
unchanged. Standard binaries and MCP remain read-only.

Version 3.20 adds exact or maximum stock sizing and read-only portfolio planning
against explicit, expiring owner targets. Routine monitoring reuses verified
statement and order-history work to reduce CPU use. The drawdown brake refuses
risk-adding orders while engaged or when required evidence is unavailable.
Desk mandate records and request lookup do not expose execution submission or
activate automatic trading. Standard binaries and MCP remain read-only.

Version 3.19 adds owner-approved currency repayments, gated bill and bond orders
by ISIN or CUSIP, and bond yield, duration and rate-risk measurements. Currency
leveling starts disabled and cannot be pre-authorised. Bond-risk measurements
introduce no new warnings or blocks. Cash settings and risk presets are served
from the daemon; order-limit changes require verified device confirmation.
Qualifying exits can pass the notional and option-contract caps only when they
reduce absolute net delta for both their underlying and the portfolio, fit
beside working orders and satisfy the option-cover checks. This also applies
to existing pre-authorised exit buckets, with their notice and veto window.
Existing written policy limits are preserved; newly written defaults are 10%
of net liquidation value and 10 option contracts. Standard binaries and MCP
remain read-only.

Version 3.18 introduced the following features. It shows every limit in force and checks that the limits add up.
`canary policy show --explain` prints every limit, policy and runtime setting
that governs Canary, each with its value, unit, source and meaning, and `canary
policy show SECTION` prints one part. `canary policy check` reads the config and
the policy files against each other and, through the daemon, against the live
account (`--offline` checks the files alone), and names each implausible value
with a reason and, where one applies, a suggested fix. MCP clients get the same
report from the read-only `canary_policy_check` tool, which never changes a
limit. The per-order limits now live in the risk constitution,
`risk-policy.toml` `[order_limits]`, and the order-value cap scales with net
liquidation value between a floor and ceiling in the policy file. A temporary
larger cap is one override that Canary records in its journal. The cash sweep's
reserve follows net liquidation value and planned needs, each bill order stays
between a minimum and a maximum size and bill buys wait while any currency is
borrowed. The daemon now produces the portfolio stress verdict and the position
risk flags; the CLI, MCP tools, app and Go client show the installed daemon's
answer. `canary setups coverage`, `options` and `markouts` print readable output
by default (`--json` returns the previous output), and the status, market,
macro, proposal and data-health views lead with what needs attention. In trading
builds the order-value cap and the short-sale check no longer refuse a
broker-side stop that, with the other working sell orders for the same stock or
ETF, sells no more than the long position, and a protective stop guard writes on
its own, but only to shrink or cancel stop orders Canary itself placed when the
position falls below them. Stops placed by hand are never changed. Version 3.18.1
introduced automatic policy migration: at its first start the daemon backs up
each file it changes and writes the missing keys. That release wrote a 5% of
net liquidation scale with a 100,000 base-currency ceiling. Version 3.19 writes
10% and 10 option contracts only for new or missing keys; existing written
values are preserved and the 100,000 ceiling is unchanged. The sweep remains off by default. Owner commissioning requires
calibrated reserves and current native settlement evidence; missing evidence
holds the sweep. Bills can lose value on an early sale. Standard binaries and
the MCP server remain read-only. Installation does not enable automatic
submission or grant broker-write permission.

Canary is a local risk desk for a brokerage account, built as a Go daemon, a
shell CLI, a read-only stdio MCP server, a Claude Desktop MCPB, a Claude Code
plugin, a paired app, and a clean-room TWS protocol library. It works with
Interactive Brokers today (IB Gateway or TWS); the broker layer is a separate
Go package, `github.com/osauer/canary/v3/pkg/ibkr`, so other platforms can
follow. The daemon owns the broker connection, account scope, runtime state,
data-source health, market sensors, rulebook, protection proposals, and
option-exercise opportunities. Other surfaces adapt that typed authority rather
than recreating it.

Canary is an independent personal project by Oliver Sauer.

Canary v3.17.0 adds a durable owner watchlist, read-only volume-turn
observations, standard-call discovery, setup coverage and entry markouts through
the CLI and typed Go reads. Setup parameters are unvalidated observations, and
historical reconstruction does not establish what was known at the original
decision. Markouts use later quotes for qualifying Canary-placed fills, exclude
commissions and never replace account P/L; missed targets stay missing. These
setup tools have no MCP surface. Watchlist edits change local preferences only.
CLI and read-only MCP add indicative borrowing-rate discovery, dated price and
liquidity context, and FINRA short-interest screens. Borrower costs are not
lender yields. FINRA positions are twice-monthly reports; percentage of free
float remains unavailable. Source dates and partial market coverage stay visible.

Canary v3.16.0 adds lending observations to the signed binaries and MCPB.
The read-only `canary lending fees --json` command and `canary_lending_fees`
MCP tool expose bounded customer net-fee history from retained IBKR statements. The app shows
dated position loan annotations and expandable fees; Desk's analyst can read
the same evidence. Missing sections, partial coverage and complete zero are
distinct. Participation stays with IBKR. Fees are not added to account P&L:
payment status and P&L/accrual linkage remain unproved. Populated account reports
are still needed for commissioning. Borrow Fee Details describes short-borrow
costs; it is not earned lending income. Forex P&L Details describes currency
transactions and realised lots; it is not the valuation contribution reported
by `canary reporting fx`.
See https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/understand/edge.html#stock-lending-income.

Canary v3.16.0 adds FX contribution to the signed binaries and MCPB.
`canary reporting fx`, `canary_reporting_fx` and Desk's Portfolio → Performance
→ FX expose the same result.
It attributes completed statement-day P&L to currencies in the account's base
currency for Day, WTD, MTD and YTD. It reconciles FX plus other P&L to portfolio
value change after external flows. Partial periods expose missing dates and
omit totals; this is valuation attribution, not realised tax-lot P&L.
See https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/start/reporting.html#fx-contribution.

Data comes from the user's own TWS or IB Gateway session. Availability and
freshness therefore depend on session state, market hours, broker entitlements,
and upstream sources. A delayed, held, fallback, partial, or unavailable result
must retain its data quality, warning code, freshness, source health, and session
context; returning a value does not make a fallback green.

The public project home is https://osauer.dev/canary/. The source repository is
https://github.com/osauer/canary.

## Safety boundary

Standard installer, MCPB, and plain `canary` downloads contain no compiled
broker-write path. The MCP server has no settings-write, order-preview, order
placement, modification, cancellation, or exercise tools, and no resource
subscriptions.

The separate opt-in `canary-trading` tarballs add constrained CLI and app broker
actions. A trading action still requires the matching build, verified account
and mode pins, fresh confirmation or preflight where applicable, journal health,
daemon authorization, and `trading.freeze=false`. No release command or agent
instruction grants a broker write. Trading builds also support explicitly pre-authorised defensive proposals within the existing policy and execution gates.
Since v3.18, a protective stop guard in trading builds writes on its own, but
only shrinks or cancels stop orders Canary itself placed when the position falls
below them. Stops placed by hand are never changed. A freeze holds a shrink but
not a cancel, and every other write gate still applies.

## Install and version lines

Product v3 installs from signed release assets:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osauer/canary/main/install.sh | sh
canary setup claude-desktop
```

The public Go module is `github.com/osauer/canary/v3` from v3.38.0: its root
package is the daemon client, `canarytest` its test double, and `pkg/ibkr` the
TWS wire protocol. Every release tag is a Go module version, so a Go program
gets the client at the release its daemon runs,
`go get github.com/osauer/canary/v3@vX.Y.Z`, and `@latest` is the newest
release. The `/v2` path ends at v2.8.5. Use the installer or signed release
assets for the binary.

The updater stays within the installed product major. Stable v2 maintenance is
cut from `release/2.x`; product v3 and later are cut from `main`.

## MCP tools

Run the server with `canary mcp`. It exposes these read-only tools:

- `canary_status`: daemon, gateway, storage, and source health.
- `canary_data_health`: passive service-health report with source clocks, restrictions and retry state; paginate with its revision.
- `canary_data_check`: coalesced bounded check of required ordinary quote feeds; no subscription purchases or settings changes.
- `canary_trading_status`: pinned broker-write readiness and blockers.
- `canary_settings`: platform settings and observed data quality; no writes.
- `canary_orders_open`: current-context local order lifecycle.
- `canary_orders_history`: bounded local order-journal history.
- `canary_order_status`: typed lifecycle evidence for one journaled order.
- `canary_account`: account financials with field-level authority.
- `canary_positions`: held positions and exposure with account authority.
- `canary_portfolio`: signed allocation by asset class and GICS sector as a share of net liquidation, with index-fund look-through and valuation coverage.
- `canary_recon_status`: redacted statement acquisition and reconciliation health.
- `canary_market`: benchmark and held-underlying quotes with actual contract identity.
- `canary_market_history`: bounded observed underlying bars for charts.
- `canary_calendar`: exchange sessions, holidays, and upcoming closures.
- `canary_macro`: cached official economic calendars and publications with source health.
- `canary_strategies`: current held-option strategy grouping; no order actions.
- `canary_technical`: daily technical evidence for explicitly named symbols.
- `canary_regime`: all eight market indicators, cluster confirmation, and source health.
- `canary_stress`: full portfolio-stress assessment with risk evidence and source health.
- `canary_brief`: current daemon-composed desk summary and Action Queue.
- `canary_reporting`: redacted broker-reporting setup and evidence status.
- `canary_reporting_performance`: retained statement equity series with dated external flows and year-to-date income sums; computes no return.
- `canary_reporting_fx` (since v3.16.0): completed statement-day FX contribution, period coverage and dated gaps; read-only, with no backfill trigger.
- `canary_lending_fees` (since v3.16.0): bounded earned net-fee history, with coverage and unproved payment/P&L linkage; no broker changes.
- `canary_lending_rates`: dated indicative borrower costs for explicitly named US stocks; not earned lender income.
- `canary_lending_screen`: broader borrowing-fee discovery with filters before the result limit, source dates and coverage.
- `canary_lending_market`: bounded cached price and liquidity context; partial or unavailable fields retain their source clocks.
- `canary_short_interest_screen`: FINRA reported short shares and days to cover, with twice-monthly settlement dates; no percentage of free float.
- `canary_edge`: retrospective decision impact for stocks, ETFs and options, a verdict on each stock and ETF decision, one grade per closed option position, and separate option actuals.
- `canary_rules`: ranked rulebook findings, explicit unknown inputs, and the limits in force with their source.
- `canary_policy_check` (since v3.18.0): plausibility check of config.toml and the policy files against each other and the live book; each finding has a severity, the keys involved, a reason and, where one applies, a suggested fix. Read-only; it never changes a limit.
- `canary_proposals`: read-only close/reduce protection candidates.
- `canary_opportunities`: read-only held-option exercise candidates.

Breadth, gamma, and corporate-event engines remain internal daemon inputs.
Regime and Stress provide detailed CLI/MCP reads, while Brief remains the summary.
Regime/Stress history is still retired. The full policy view and detailed
reconciliation reads remain CLI-only governance surfaces; MCP provides the policy
plausibility check and reconciliation status.

## CLI workflow

Useful read-only commands include:

```sh
canary status
canary account
canary positions --by underlying
canary technical AAPL,MSFT
canary brief
canary regime --explain
canary stress --details
canary rules
canary rules policy
canary policy show
canary policy check         # since v3.18.0
canary recon show
canary reporting fx --json # since v3.16.0
canary lending fees --json  # since v3.16.0
canary watchlist list --json
canary setups coverage --json
canary setups markouts --json
canary lending screen --json
canary short-interest screen --json
canary strategies list
canary proposals list
canary opportunities list
canary orders open
canary settings
```

The generated CLI reference is the command authority. The app adds the morning
brief and converged Action Queue, current and recovered alerts, constrained order
surfaces, option-exercise confirmation, data-quality disclosure, settings, and
mobile navigation.

## Requirements

- macOS or Linux; Windows is supported through WSL only.
- IB Gateway 10.37+ or TWS running locally with TWS API access enabled.
- IBKR market-data entitlements for real-time sources the workflow needs.

The daemon auto-discovers common local ports and uses a local Unix-socket RPC
surface. Raw account identifiers and broker credentials do not go to a hosted
Canary service.

Good descriptions say Canary reports the evidence currently available and names
what is stale, degraded, held, blocked, or unknown. Do not claim a fallback is
live, that an MCP client has order authority, that a v3 product tag makes the
`/v2` Go module v3, or that an app/CLI review authorizes a trade.
